G3-6 · Native feasibility spikes · results

Results · G3-6 still openNo E board changed · 6 Nov 2026

You authorised two isolated spikes: a native iPhone/iPad tab bar over Flutter content, and a native Mac sidebar under a transparent Flutter layer. Every image below is a genuine capture from those test apps. Simulator results do not prove real-device behaviour; those items are marked.

How it was tested

  • Isolation: two throwaway Flutter 3.47.8 sample apps in the session scratchpad, outside the Dottoday repo and worktree; no packages; synthetic tasks only. Nothing in app/, Supabase, hosting, auth or dependencies changed.
  • iPhone / iPad: two simulators created only for this (“G36 Spike iPhone”, iPhone 17 Pro; “G36 Spike iPad”, iPad Pro 11-inch M5; iOS 26.5), deleted afterwards. The simulators already running were not touched.
  • N1 · native root: UITabBarController (iOS 18 UITab API) is the root; one Flutter view is hosted behind all tabs; selection, badge and safe-area insets go over a platform channel.
  • N2 · bar over Flutter: Flutter is the root; a native UITabBar sits in a UiKitView platform view at the bottom.
  • Mac: release build on this Mac (MacBook Pro, Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26.6.2, 120 Hz). NSVisualEffectView (sidebar material, behind-window) under a transparent Flutter view. A synthetic striped window sits behind the test window so captures never include your desktop; two timing runs without it had their captures deleted unseen.
  • Not used: your iPhone (iOS 27.0.1, paired). Installing needs code signing, which needs your approval. Every iPhone/iPad result here is simulator-only; physical-device validation is outstanding.

7 · Deviations from approved Concept E

  • iPhone tab bar: Apple draws it (shape, selection lens, SF labels, red badge). Close to E-Phones' drawing; not identical. Labels do not grow with Dynamic Type, unlike E's drawn bar.
  • Search: kept inside the capsule as on E-Phones by using a regular tab; Apple's own apps put it in a separate circle.
  • iPad: native tabs move to the top and can become a sidebar. E has no approved iPad layout yet (Round 2), so this is input for Round 2, not a conflict.
  • Mac sidebar: neutral system material instead of E's warm tinted sidebar.
  • Android and web: untouched.

8 · Recommendation per component

  • iPhone native tab bar: worth pursuing with N1 (native root, Flutter hosted behind, insets and state bridged), Search as a regular tab to keep E's layout. Before adopting: device test (VoiceOver, keyboard, performance, touch), and a decision on iOS 16–17 (classic tab API path, or raise the minimum to iOS 18). Not N2: dropped-tap risk, non-native iPad placement, screen-reader path unproven.
  • Other iPhone chrome (Day chip, capsules, menus): keep in Flutter for now (approximated, with solid fallback); a native Day menu (UIMenu) is a later, separate test.
  • iPad native navigation: take N1's top tab bar with optional sidebar as the starting direction for Round 2 iPad design; needs its own designs.
  • Mac sidebar: feasible and cheap: genuine vibrancy behind a transparent Flutter view, no measurable cost. Remaining: VoiceOver and keyboard check on your Mac, and whether to warm-tint the material.
  • Android and web: unchanged (Material 3; solid web).
  • Nothing adopted: G3-6 stays open for your decision.
